A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, authors, generation pipeline, and core experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and visual inspection supports reliable comparison of figures, tables, and equations.

before.justification: V1 reports original PolitiFact analyses, RoBERTa fine-tuning results, and experiments evaluating iteratively generated fake news.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds Snopes evaluation, comparisons with earlier generated-news datasets, detector ablations, and human fact-checking results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Equation 1, and all supplied prompts are unchanged. Candidate generation, contradiction/edit filtering, plausibility ranking, and iterative RAG feedback remain the same; v2 clarifies model roles without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: V2 adds 3,212 Snopes items from January 2016 to October 2024 and evaluates machine-generated GossipCop and PolitiFact datasets from Su et al. and Chen and Shu. This substantially broadens the evaluated sources and generated-news coverage beyond v1's retained PolitiFact, LIAR, and NBC-based experiments.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 introduces empirical generation comparisons using released outputs from Su et al. (2023b) and Chen and Shu (2024), which v1 only cited. The principal generated-news and LIAR detector rosters remain unchanged. The balanced PolitiFact comparison now shows two backbones instead of six, while the six-backbone unbalanced comparison remains in the appendix.

E3.justification: V2 adds Average Precision reporting (Table 12), a shuffled, unpaired, label-hidden 100-example human check with Google access (Section 3.1), and controlled temperature and wording comparisons (Tables 10–11). These extend evaluation procedures without establishing a redesign or rerun of the retained core experiments.

E4.justification: Tables 10–11 add limited analyses testing temperature-1 score averaging against temperature-0 prediction and 'plausibility' against 'factuality' prompts across event periods. The blinded human check adds fact-checkability evidence. Existing feedback ablations, PolitiFact attribute analyses, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average multiple temperature-1 predictions without specifying experimental run counts or seeds. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run uncertainty estimates; the new sampling ablation concerns detector settings.

E6.justification: V2 adds Snopes temporal findings, earlier-dataset scores (Table 3), 99% human performance on 100 examples, detector-ablation results, and AP scores. Matched core results remain unchanged: GPT-4o with News retrieval has first/last-round AUCs of 82.4/64.9 in both v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1. The new cross-dataset results are additional comparisons, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The binary classification formulation and argmax selection equation remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical proofs or theorems; the added plausibility discussion and source-reliability caveat do not alter formal reasoning.

C1.justification: V2 expands the principal diagnosis from increasingly easy political claims to distinct problems involving source selection, pre-training contamination, and retrieval leakage across PolitiFact and Snopes. Its introduction also adds an explicit contribution claim that the generated datasets challenge detectors more than previous neural fake-news datasets. The central iterative-generation and RAG claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes PolitiFact shortcut patterns from possible contamination and retrieval-label leakage on Snopes. It revises the explanation of erroneous RAG confidence toward distraction or mistrust of external context, and adds substantive limitations concerning NBC's reliability and fabricated details without retrievable evidence (Sections 2.2, 5.1, and 8).

D1.justification: V2 provides a code/data repository link instead of only promising release, identifies GPT-4o's pipeline roles, states the final 402/402 dataset composition and score normalization, and documents Snopes acquisition and baseline sample sizes. Some earlier preprocessing descriptions, including anonymous-post and non-news filtering, disappear. Model-version information and several retrieval details are relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds Huang et al. (2024b), Lucas et al. (2023), and Shahi and Nandini (2020). It also credits Pelrine et al. with similar PolitiFact findings, softening v1's 'first comprehensive analysis' positioning. The main distinction from one-round generation remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and background are substantially rewritten around two fact-checking sources and an explicit contribution list. Dataset creation becomes Section 3.1, experimental setup is reorganized, and RoBERTa and retrieval details move into an expanded appendix. These materially change the narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: V2 redraws and relocates the pipeline schematic, replaces the original PolitiFact overview with a two-source figure, and merges the main result table with the iteration plot. New comparison, ablation, and AP tables accompany extensive rearrangement of appendix displays; some model and example information is reformatted from existing material.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked blinded human fact-checkability testing and quantitative comparisons with earlier generation outputs. V2 adds both (Section 3.1 and Table 3), substantially strengthening evidence for the benchmark's usefulness beyond paired rewrite inspection. The Snopes analysis and explicit limitations also improve the scope of its conclusions. Cross-dataset comparisons still do not isolate generation-method effects from source and date differences, but the added validation provides a clear substantial net benefit.
